claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: For example, binary word 101 belongs to the target n=3 factor family but is not periodically admissible under forbidding 11, so Moreno–Matamala’s Euler tour does not cover our target. Cutting an optimal cycle requires up to n−1 letters to display boundary-crossing factors and does not turn Wang–Shallit’s linear result into this exact minimum. The present claim is a strict all-order extension beyond finite optimizer enumerations; it does not claim novelty for their known finite length values.

originality.rationale: Full primary text comparison distinguishes Wang–Shallit’s exact LINEAR Fibonacci length, Tan–Shallit’s generic shortest circular witness bounds, and Moreno–Matamala’s lexicographically minimal cyclic language restricted to periodically admissible factors. None implies the claimed all-order minimum for every internally admissible factor, including words such as 101. Earlier finite optimal-length values are acknowledged as already known. The result may still have unindexed anticipation.

value.rationale: This is a natural exact period invariant for covering all factors of the canonical golden-mean shift, settled simultaneously for infinitely many lengths with constructive Eulerian paths. The sharp extra F_n−1 factor repetitions quantify a structural non-Eulerian obstruction, making it more than a routine finite enumeration or relabeling. It is a motivated exact classification of minimal lengths, not an optimizer count or unsupported downstream consequence.
